Step 1 of 3

Choose an AI to write your summaries

This extension reads a video's captions, but it doesn't write the summary itself. It hands the transcript to an AI of your choosing. Google's is free.

A ChatGPT Plus or Claude Pro subscription doesn't include an API key — those are billed separately. If that's all you have, take the free option.

It's a long password that lets this extension use your Google account's AI — and nothing else. Google hands them out free.

It is stored in this browser, on this computer. It isn't sent to whoever made this extension; there is no server here for it to go to. Delete it whenever you like and summaries simply stop.

    Keys stay in this browser and are sent only to the provider they belong to. The transcript goes to whichever provider generates the summary — with Auto, that is any provider you have configured here, including for members-only videos. Summarizing happens on the provider's servers unless you point a custom provider at a local endpoint.

    Time saved is an estimate: each video’s length minus how long its summary takes to read, at about 200 words a minute. It never counts below zero, and it is arithmetic on your own counter rather than a measurement of you.

    About
    There is no server of mine. Your keys, preferences and statistics live in this browser’s local storage — and only the extension’s own pages can read them, not the YouTube page.

    What leaves this computer

    The transcriptOnly when you press Generate
    to your AI
    Your keyAs the header that authorises the request
    with it
    Everything elsePreferences, statistics, what you watch
    nowhere

    Summarizing runs on the provider’s servers — a key living on your machine is not the same as AI running on it. With more than one AI configured, Auto sends the transcript to the next one when the first fails, members-only videos included.

    Sites this extension can reach

    youtube.com generativelanguage.googleapis.com api.openai.com api.anthropic.com

    Adding your own endpoint asks Chrome for that one host, and removing it hands the access back. Remote endpoints must use https — plain http is allowed only for localhost.

    Captions

    When YouTube’s transcript panel is unavailable, the extension reads the caption track the player already loaded for the video you are watching. Those responses stay in that page’s memory — at most four tracks, cleared as soon as you navigate — and go nowhere except to your chosen AI, as the transcript.
